top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces or aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, KLOwen, Lightforce, SmartSTL, self-ligating braces, Twin brackets, damon ultima brackets, SLB, Aliwell
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, rentability, staff efficiency, diary changes, practice optimisation, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in second and third order movements, decrease of emergencies, dynamic scheduling, practice differentiation
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually save them time or money, or that it will meaningfully reduce appointments or chair time. They question whether the investment in DM will pay off, especially for braces, and want proof of efficiency and financial benefit before changing workflows.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, white paper, peer-reviewed, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
Are Damon brackets more efficient than other brands?
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct, recent, and region-specific ROI and efficiency data for DM with braces and aligners is often lacking, especially for non-Invisalign brands and for large/multi-location practices. More robust, comparative studies and real-world financial outcomes should be prioritized.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI for clinical observations and remote monitoring
top_needs.brands_and_products: SmartSTL, Spark, Damon, self-ligating braces, intraoralscan
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of AI detecting malocclusions, accuracy of AI detecting eruption, accuracy of AI vs orthodontist, accuracy of scanning, accuracy class I goal, accuracy of smartphone-based monitoring, accuracy of SmartSTL AI, accuracy of AI for refinement, FDA class I
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI is accurate enough to reliably detect clinical issues, track treatment progress, or replace in-person assessments. Some are concerned about regulatory validation and want to see head-to-head comparisons with human clinicians.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, white paper, peer-reviewed, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for more peer-reviewed, quantitative studies directly comparing DM’s AI to orthodontists and validating its accuracy for specific clinical tasks, especially for regulatory and skeptical audiences.
